en: to be hit; to get rained on

examples.en: I didn't have an umbrella, so I got rained on.
My leg that got hit by the ball still hurts.
I walked to school in the snow.
I got hit by a ball that flew at me, and it hurt.
Don't get rained on. Come over this way.

examples.ko: 갑자기 비를 맞아서 옷이 다 젖었어요.
examples.en: I suddenly got rained on, and my clothes are all wet.

explain: '비를 맞다, 눈을 맞다'는 '을/를'과 함께 쓰고, '공에 맞다, 돌에 맞다'는 '에'와 함께 써요. 때리는 쪽은 '때리다', 맞는 쪽은 '맞다'예요. '답이 맞다'의 '맞다'와 모양과 활용이 같아서('맞아요') 조사와 문맥으로 구분해요.

phrases.example: 갑자기 소나기를 맞아서 옷이 다 젖었어요.
phrases.en: I got caught in a sudden shower, and my clothes got soaked.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑자기 내리는 비를 피하지 못하고 맞았을 때 쓴다.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you could not avoid a sudden downpour and got rained on.

explain_en: '비를 맞다' and '눈을 맞다' take 을/를, while '공에 맞다' and '돌에 맞다' take 에. The one who hits is '때리다' and the one who gets hit is '맞다'. It looks and conjugates the same as '맞다' (to be correct), so tell them apart by the particle and context.

examples.en: I welcome guests at the front door with a smile.

examples.ko: 엄마가 문 앞에서 저를 반갑게 맞아 주셨어요.
examples.en: Mom greeted me warmly at the door.
We welcomed the new year together with our family.

examples.ko: 새 학기를 맞아서 새 가방을 샀어요.
examples.en: To welcome the new semester, I bought a new bag.
To welcome the new spring, I cleaned the house.
The staff are greeting guests at the entrance.

explain: 손님, 새해, 봄, 새 학기처럼 사람이나 때를 맞이할 때 써요. '맞이하다'와 같은 뜻인데 '맞다'가 더 짧아요. 떠나는 손님은 '배웅하다'라고 하고, 공항에 사람을 데리러 나갈 때는 보통 '마중 나가다'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 우리 가족은 새해를 맞아 여행을 갔어요.
phrases.en: My family went on a trip to welcome the new year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새해나 명절 같은 때를 기쁘게 맞이할 때 쓴다.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when happily welcoming a time such as the new year or a holiday.

explain_en: Use it to welcome people or a time, such as guests, the new year, spring or a new semester. It means the same as '맞이하다' but is shorter. For seeing a guest off you say '배웅하다', and for going out to pick someone up you usually say '마중 나가다'.
